title: CompliA
summary: An AI assistant inside Telefónica's compliance portal: it answers in natural language, analyses declarations and helps issue rulings. I designed and built it: the RAG, the validations, the restrictions and the recommendations.

facts.v: Design and development, end to end
RAG assistant on top of a language model

tldr.v: A lot of compliance information, old and new, and processes that need judgement: declarations, forms, rulings and reports.
An assistant that searches the documents, answers with that context and stays bounded by rules: it states its limits and leaves the ruling to a person.
It runs in internal production. I don't show metrics or data: they belong to Telefónica.

p: Telefónica's compliance portal digitalises internal processes, improves traceability and supports end-to-end flows: declarations, forms, interactions and administrative operations.
I work on it at Tsoft as a Ssr AI Fullstack Developer. CompliA is its conversational assistant.

list: Answers in natural language about historical and new compliance data.
Analyses sworn declarations and flags possible conflicts of interest and breaches of the programme's rules.
Helps issue rulings, assigns forms and builds the programme's reports.
States its limits: it can make mistakes and some processes need human action.

p: A RAG assistant doesn't answer from memory: first it finds what matters in the documents, and only then does the language model write with that context. Rules decide what it may answer and when a person has to step in.

diagram.title: From a question to a reviewed answer
diagram.caption: Generic scheme of a RAG assistant like CompliA. It is not Telefónica's architecture: no system names, data, controls or providers.

search.label: Search
search.note: Brings only the passages that matter for that question: that is the RAG.

llm.label: Language model
llm.note: Just one component: it writes from what was retrieved.

rules.label: Validations
rules.note: They bound what it may answer and when it must hand over to a person.

human.label: Human review
human.note: The assistant helps issue the ruling; a person confirms it.

p: The language model is one component; what makes it useful and safe in compliance are these four pieces.

steps.d: Locate, in the compliance data, what each question needs.
Every answer meets the rules before it is shown.
What the assistant doesn't do alone: some processes need human action.
Issue rulings, assign forms and build reports.

p: I designed and built all of it: the RAG, the validations, the restrictions and the recommendations.
On the same portal I work end to end: frontend, backend, CI/CD and integrations.
In compliance, an assistant that is confidently wrong is worse than no assistant. That's why the limits are part of the product.

items.d: It warns that it can make mistakes and that some processes need human action.
It helps issue the ruling, but a person confirms it.
It writes from what it finds in the documents, not from memory.
Validations and restrictions run before anything reaches the screen.
